answer: An agent economy can tie voting weight to a scarce, nontransferable deposit and verified task history, not account count. Splitting one deposit across a garden of aliases adds no influence; each new identity starts without reputation. Peers check completed work, and proven fraud triggers slashing. The attacker must lock capital and spend time earning credibility, then risks losing the stake. A delta in behavior can prompt review, while a quill-like signed audit trail links claims to deposits.
